To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the quality of a distance learning program can be improved by a well designed combination of the pedagogical gesture of tutoring, with the use of ICT, which includes an appropriate use of the Internet.
the following three aspects of the tutoring process have the greatest impact on student performance: 1.

(1) the use of a Web-based system that supports the development of collaborative skills and that provides opportunities for students to reflect on their learning is associated with higher levels of self-efficacy; (2) students with high levels of self-efficiency are more likely to use a Web-based system to support their learning; and (3) the use of the Web-based system to facilitate the development of collaborative and reflective skills may contribute to the development of self-efficacious learners.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and evaluation of computer tools to help tutors and students in the context of distance education.
the industrialization of tutoring in distance learning.
the development of a pedagogical approach to distance learning, based upon the use of computer-mediated tools.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the tutor is the most important factor in the distance learning process, but the use of ICT is also a factor which must be taken into account in order to achieve the quality of distance teaching.
the industrialization of tutoring is possible but that it must be done with care and in a context of a pedagogical approach.

the tutor is an essential element in the distance learning process, and that the quality of this process depends on the quality of the interaction between the tutor and the learner, and between the tutor and all the tools and resources available to him/her.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of ICTs for distance education is not only a technical matter but a pedagogical matter as well.
the quality of distance education depends not only on technical aspects but also on the pedagogical aspects.
the tutor is a central element of distance education and that his pedagogical gesture should be supported by the use of information and communication technologies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of information technology to support distance teaching should not be considered as an end in itself, but rather as a means to enhance the teaching/learning process.
the tutor's pedagogical gestures are a key factor for the quality of the distance learning process.
it is important for tutors to use tools which support the learners in their knowledge acquisition process.
